You are the route and logistics specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose the legs this trip is made of — drives, rides, transfers, ferries and trains — with the stops that make a long one bearable.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is a movement, so its location is {"kind":"between","from":{...},"to":{...}} with **both** ends as places. Endpoints in the title are not endpoints, and a candidate that puts them there is discarded.
- This trip has 9 days.
- **Nothing you propose may be longer than 300 minutes.** That is the party's own answer about how much a day holds, translated into minutes. Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

candidates.title: Drive down the St. Lawrence south shore to Kamouraska
candidates.summary: About 4 hours of driving on Autoroute 20, longer with stops. Break it at Lévis or Montmagny so the seven-year-old is never more than 2–3 hours in the car. Access needs were not answered, so rest-stop accessibility is not accounted for.

candidates.title: Coast road from Kamouraska into the Haute-Gaspésie
candidates.summary: Follows Route 132 past Rimouski and Matane to where the coast turns wild and new to you. Reford Gardens at Grand-Métis or the Matane waterfront make natural midway breaks.

candidates.title: Northern Gaspé coast drive to Forillon National Park
candidates.summary: This is the most dramatic stretch of Route 132, with cliffs and small fishing villages. It is winding and slow, so stop at Mont-Saint-Pierre or the lighthouse at La Martre to break it up. Park entry fees are not included.

candidates.title: Short hop from Forillon around Gaspé Bay to Percé
candidates.summary: An easy, short drive for the child, with views over the bay. It connects your two must-see stops.

candidates.title: Baie-des-Chaleurs coast drive from Percé to Carleton-sur-Mer
candidates.summary: Takes the gentler south coast so the loop does not retrace its steps. Bonaventure or Paspébiac are good mid-drive stretches.

candidates.title: Matapédia Valley crossing back to the St. Lawrence
candidates.summary: An inland river-valley route that closes the loop, with Amqui as a midway stop. The remaining drive from Rimouski to Montréal is about 5.5 hours. That is over your half-day limit, so it must be split, for example at Rivière-du-Loup or Québec City; it is not covered by this candidate.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple family motel room in Percé puts the party within walking distance of the rock and the Bonaventure Island boats. July is peak season, so book well ahead. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Camping Des-Rosiers, Forillon National Park
candidatesAccepted.summary: A Parks Canada campground inside Forillon with serviced sites and shower buildings, close to the beaches and trails, and well within the party's 'simple' threshold. July sites go fast on the reservation system. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: oTENTik tent-cabin in Forillon
candidatesAccepted.summary: A Parks Canada tent-cabin with beds is a simple, gear-light stay with the kids inside Forillon, near shower buildings. Inventory is small, so book early. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Cottage or motel in Carleton-sur-Mer
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple stop on the Baie-des-Chaleurs south shore gives the loop new ground beyond the north shore they already know, with calm beaches for the children. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel stopover in Rivière-du-Loup

candidatesAccepted.title: Smoked fish tasting at a Gaspé smokehouse
candidatesAccepted.summary: Fumoir Monsieur Émile in Rivière-au-Renard is a working smokehouse near Forillon. Kids can see how it is done and the family can pick up picnic food. Dietary restrictions were not answered, so check fish suitability. Accessibility was also not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Seafood shack lunch in Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A casual casse-croûte serving lobster rolls, fish and chips, or a seafood plate, with views toward Percé Rock. It is relaxed enough for a 7-year-old. Food restrictions and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Fresh fish counter picnic in Gaspé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A poissonnerie (fish market) in Gaspé is a place to buy ready-to-eat shrimp, crab or smoked salmon for a picnic at a Forillon lookout. It keeps costs down on a tight budget. Food restrictions were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bakery stop in Kamouraska
candidatesAccepted.summary: A village bakery in Kamouraska on the south-shore road out is a natural leg-stretch break for the youngest. Pastries and bread for the road. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Microbrewery pub dinner in Carleton-sur-Mer
candidatesAccepted.summary: A family-friendly brewpub meal on the Baie-des-Chaleurs side of the loop, which is new ground for a family who have done the north shore. It serves local food and has kid options. Food restrictions were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park day entry and family trails
candidatesAccepted.summary: Covers the requested Forillon visit: short coastal trails like Cap-Gaspé suit an 11- and 7-year-old at moderate effort. The band assumes Parks Canada daily family/group admission, not a Discovery Pass. Access needs were not answered, so trail suitability is unchecked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Boat cruise to Bonaventure Island from Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: Gives a close view of the requested Percé Rock plus the gannet colony, with an optional island walk. The band assumes a standard cruise for two adults and two children, and may or may not include SÉPAQ park entry; this is unconfirmed. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Parc national de la Gaspésie short visit
candidatesAccepted.summary: An inland stop on the south-to-north loop that breaks up driving for the 7-year-old. The band assumes SÉPAQ day access for two adults, with children free. Season and access were not verified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Serviced campsite or cabin night in a SÉPAQ park
candidatesAccepted.summary: A low-cost simple night with showers, which respects their limit of no more than one night without showers. The band is for one night, either a serviced site or a ready-to-camp tent, for four people. Peak July demand means booking early; availability is unchecked. Access needs were not answered.
